metaTitle: Lis Pendens: Selling Disputed Land in Bangladesh
title: Lis Pendens: Selling Disputed Land in Bangladesh
metaDescription: Learn how Section 52 of the Transfer of Property Act 1882 (Lis Pendens) blocks buyers of disputed land in Bangladesh during a pending civil suit.
keywords: buying disputed land pending suit Bangladesh
heroIntro: Under Section 52 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 (the doctrine of Lis Pendens), any immovable property that is the subject of a pending, non-collusive civil suit cannot be transferred so as to affect the rights of any other party to the decree. A purchaser who buys disputed land during litigation is automatically bound by the final court judgment.

quickAnswer.heading: At a Glance: Doctrine of Lis Pendens (Section 52)
points: Governing Statute: Section 52 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 & Order 39 Rules 1–2 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.
Core Effect: A sale deed executed while a suit is pending is not void by itself, but remains strictly subservient to the final decree.
No Notice Required: Unlike equitable doctrines, Section 52 binds subsequent buyers even if they had no actual knowledge of the pending suit.
Preventive Step: Pair Section 52 protection with a Temporary Injunction (Order 39) and Sub-Registry notice to stop physical transfer.

sections.h2: What Is Lis Pendens Under Section 52 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882?
sections.content:
Section 52 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 codifies the common-law maxim pendente lite nihil innovetur—meaning nothing new should be introduced into a pending litigation. When a suit or proceeding is pending in a competent Bangladeshi court in which any right to immovable property is directly and specifically in question, the property cannot be transferred or otherwise dealt with by any party so as to affect the rights of any other party under any decree or order passed therein.

For Non-Resident Bangladeshis (NRBs) and resident landowners, this rule prevents an unscrupulous co-sharer or trespasser from defeating a partition suit or deed cancellation suit simply by selling the disputed land to a third party mid-trial. Even if the new buyer registers a Saf Kabala deed and obtains mutation, the final court decree binds that transferee just as if they were a party from day one.

Always verify pending litigation before purchasing property in Dhaka; consult a dedicated land lawyer in Bangladesh or review our Dhaka land buying legal guide.

sections.h2: Conditions Required for Lis Pendens Protection in Bangladesh
sections.content:
Bangladeshi civil courts and the Supreme Court require five cumulative conditions under Section 52 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 before a transfer pendente lite is subordinated to a decree:

Statutory ConditionLegal Requirement Under Section 52Common Pitfall to Avoid
Active PendencySuit filed in a competent court (from plaint presentation until final execution).Transfers made before plaint registration or after suit dismissal without restoration.
Non-Collusive SuitThe litigation must be genuine and contested, not collusive between parties.Sham compromise suits staged solely to block third-party creditors.
Immovable Property in IssueTitle, possession, partition, or mortgage of the specific plot must be directly in question.Simple money recovery suits without any prayer against specific land.
Authority of Court AbsentTransfer occurs without prior written permission of the court trying the suit.Court-sanctioned sales or receiver auctions under Order 40 CPC.

Note that pendency under the Explanation to Section 52 continues through appeals and execution proceedings until full satisfaction of the decree, unless execution becomes time-barred under the Limitation Act, 1908.

sections.h2: Lis Pendens vs Temporary Injunction (Order 39 CPC)
sections.content:
While Section 52 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 automatically subordinates a mid-suit buyer's title to the eventual decree, it does not physically stop the Sub-Registrar from registering a deed or prevent a buyer from erecting structures on the plot. That is why litigants must simultaneously apply for a Temporary Injunction under Order 39 Rules 1 and 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

If a defendant sells or alters land in violation of an existing Order 39 injunction, the plaintiff can immediately move for contempt and detention/attachment of property under Order 39 Rule 2(3) CPC, whereas Section 52 alone operates only at the decree execution stage. Moreover, an Order 39 stay order delivered to the local Sub-Registry Office and AC (Land) Office alerts officials to halt mutation (Namjari) transfers.

To check whether a seller has already mutated disputed land behind your back, see our online khatian and mutation check guide and possession recovery steps.

sections.h2: Step-by-Step Procedure to Protect Disputed Land During Suit
sections.content:
If you are prosecuting a land suit or discover the defendant sold your disputed plot mid-trial, execute these five steps immediately:

  1. File Plaint with Exact Mouza & Dag Schedule: Describe the CS/SA/RS/BS Khatian, Dag numbers, and boundary measurements accurately in the plaint so Section 52 attaches unambiguously to the plot.
  2. Move Order 39 Injunction Petition: Apply on day one for a status-quo or temporary injunction restraining alienation, mortgage, or construction.
  3. Serve Certified Order on Sub-Registrar & AC (Land): Submit a certified copy of the plaint filing slip and injunction order to the Sub-Registry Office and AC (Land) Office to block secret mutation.
  4. Implead the Subsequent Buyer (Order 1 Rule 10 & Order 22 Rule 10 CPC): If a sale deed has already been registered during the suit, apply to add the transferee as a defendant so the decree binds them directly without a second lawsuit.
  5. Enforce Decree Under Order 21 Rules 97–102 CPC: Under Order 21 Rule 102, a transferee pendente lite cannot resist delivery of possession in execution; consult Advocate Md. Shah Alam for execution proceedings and check pre-emption remedies if a co-sharer sold to an outsider.

sections.h2: Documents Checklist for Challenging a Pendente Lite Sale
sections.content:
Compile these certified court and registry records when moving to bind or evict a mid-suit buyer:

  • Certified copy of the original plaint and court order-sheet showing the exact date of suit institution.
  • Certified copy (Nakal) of the subsequent Saf Kabala or Heba deed executed after the suit filing date.
  • Certified copy of any Temporary Injunction or status-quo order passed under Order 39 CPC.
  • Updated Khatian, Mutation (Namjari) order-sheet, and Land Development Tax (Khajna) receipts.
  • For NRBs abroad: an Embassy-attested Power of Attorney authorising counsel to file Order 22 Rule 10 or execution petitions.

faqs.question: Is a land sale made during a pending court case automatically void in Bangladesh?
faqs.answer: No, a transfer pendente lite under Section 52 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 is not void ab initio between the seller and buyer. However, it is legally subservient to the court's final decree, meaning if the seller loses the case, the buyer loses title to the winning party.

faqs.question: Does Lis Pendens apply if the buyer did not know about the pending lawsuit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Under Section 52 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 as applied in Bangladesh, Lis Pendens operates regardless of whether the transferee had actual or constructive notice of the pending suit. A buyer's claim of being a bona fide purchaser for value without notice cannot defeat Section 52.

faqs.question: Can a buyer who bought land during a suit stop execution of the decree?
faqs.answer: No. Under Order 21 Rule 102 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, a person to whom the judgment-debtor transferred the property after the institution of the suit cannot file an obstruction claim to resist delivery of possession in execution.

faqs.question: Does Lis Pendens protect land if the case was dismissed for default and later restored?
faqs.answer: If a suit is dismissed for default and subsequently restored under Order 9 CPC, courts generally treat the suit as continuing from its original filing date, unless a third party acquired rights bona fide during the gap before restoration was sought.

faqs.question: How can a land buyer check if a plot is subject to a pending lawsuit before buying?
faqs.answer: Buyers should commission a 12-to-25-year Sub-Registry index search, verify physical possession with neighbours, check AC (Land) mutation status, and search Civil Judge Court cause lists/record rooms in the relevant district before paying earnest money.
